key_insight: Magnetism reshapes atomic ordering in Fe-rich Fe–Si alloys: D0₃ ordering dominates in the fully ordered ferromagnetic state, while B2 ordering is promoted in the elevated-temperature paramagnetic state.
engineering_relevance: Linking magnetic state to atomic ordering can help guide composition and thermal-processing choices for Fe–Si alloys whose magnetic and mechanical properties depend on atomic arrangement.
method: Compute effective cluster interactions from density functional theory for bcc Fe–Si alloys up to 20 at% Si.
Resolve how magnetic state, lattice expansion, and Si concentration alter these interactions.
Use Monte Carlo simulations to predict temperature-dependent ordering and phase behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that simulations reproduce experimentally observed phase equilibria and short-range order characteristics, but provides no quantitative accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Predictions are demonstrated for bcc alloys up to 20 at% Si; use beyond this range requires validation.
paper_title: First-principles modeling of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys
